response.answer:
The Greater Will is described as a mysterious, supremely powerful entity or force from beyond that has great influence over the Lands Between, inhabiting a lightless void outside it; its vassals and envoys are central to the Golden Order [1]. Long ago it fractured the One Great, creating births and souls — an act the adherents of the Three Fingers consider a mistake, since it brought torment, despair, affliction, sins and curses [1]. It also sent a golden star bearing an Elden Beast into the Lands Between, which would later become the Elden Ring; that beast was its vassal and the living incarnation of the concept of Order [1][4]. Its other vassals and envoys include the Two Fingers, who speak in a sign language of light, and Metyr, mother of the Two Fingers and first shooting star to fall upon the Lands Between, who is called a daughter of the Greater Will [1].

One source goes further and speculates that the Greater Will imprisoned Queen Marika after she shattered the Elden Ring, and that on the strength of these acts it can effectively be seen as the supreme being of the Elden Ring world — but that framing is explicitly presented as speculation, not in-game confirmation [3].

response.answer:
The connection is one of parent and offspring: the Twinbird is said to be the envoy of an outer god and the mother of the Deathbirds [1][2][3]. The in-game Twinbird Kite Shield description states this directly — "The twinbird is said to be the envoy of an outer god, and mother of the Deathbirds" [4].

In the era before the Erdtree, the Deathbirds served as keepers of ghostflame, burning the dead and raking out their ashen remains; vengeful spirits arose from those cinders, and the birds were regarded by some as malevolent deities [1][2]. The Twinbird itself is scarcely mentioned and its whereabouts are unknown, with only its offspring seen throughout the Lands Between [3].

Note that most of this comes from wiki prose, with the parentage claim also appearing in item text [4]; the release metadata for several of these sources is marked unknown or only a candidate, so I can't verify a specific release assignment for them.

The Twinbird is a mysterious entity tied to the Twinbird Kite Shield and the Deathbird/Death Rite Bird lineage. The shield's lore describes the Twinbird as an envoy of the outer god that presided over the cycle of life and death before the Erdtree's age—essentially a herald of a death-and-rebirth order that predates Marika's Golden Order. Its two-headed bird imagery is echoed by the Deathbirds, which are associated with ghostflame and the burning of the dead.

Much about the Twinbird is deliberately vague: it is not a character you meet, and the game never fully explains its nature or its exact relationship to the outer god it serves. Theories linking it to the Gloam-Eyed Queen or to a broader "twin" duality theme are fan interpretation rather than confirmed lore.

Originally known as Lunar Princess Ranni, she was the daughter of Radagon, a champion of the Golden Order, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. She had two older brothers, Radahn and Rykard.
Ranni was also an Empyrean, meaning she had the potential to one day succeed Queen Marika as the divine ruler of the Lands Between. The Two Fingers chose her as a potential successor and granted her a Shadow by the name of Blaidd to be her vassal. He was approved of by Rennala, and was raised as her foster brother. Ranni grew up playing with Blaidd, and they were often accompanied by Iji, a troll blacksmith who served the Carian royals.
Led by the hand of her mother Rennala, young Ranni would encounter her Dark Moon. What she beheld was cold, dark and veiled in occult mystery. Deep in the woods, she would also encounter a snowy crone, known simply as the "Snow Witch", who would go on to become her secret mentor. She was an old witch well versed in cold-based sorceries, and she taught Ranni to fear the dark moon as she imparted her magic. The full Dark Moon, cold and leaden, would become Ranni's sigil and symbol of her power and authority.
At some point, Ranni's father would abandon her mother in order to marry Queen Marika and assume the title of second Elden Lord. Ranni and her siblings were thus raised to demigod status by their new stepmother.

response.answer:
Melina is a mysterious, burnt and spectral woman who travels with the spectral steed Torrent. She first offers the maidenless Tarnished an accord: she will act as their Finger Maiden, letting them turn runes into strength, if they bring her with them to the foot of the Erdtree; she is also searching for a purpose given to her by her mother inside the Erdtree [2].

Later, after the thorns bar entry to the Erdtree, Melina asks the Tarnished to begin a new journey to the Flame of Ruin, far above the clouds on the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants, so that the Erdtree can be burned open; she says she will handle the “kindling” needed to set it alight [1].

sources.title: Melina
sources.text:
After defeating Morgott, the Tarnished finds the path into the Erdtree barred by thorns refusing entrance to all. Melina, having ascertained her purpose and seeing the Tarnished stuck, rejoins the Tarnished to say that she can burn the Erdtree to gain entrance inside, provided that she can get ahold of the Flame of Ruin. And hence, she asks to go on a new journey, this time to the flame of ruin, far above the clouds, upon the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants. and tells them she will take care of the "kindling" required to set the tree alight.
Defeating Morgott also opens up the path to the Three Fingers. If the Tarnished rests at the nearest grace from their entombment, Melina will warn against meeting them and insist against inheriting the Frenzied Flame, for it would end all lives and births, which she cherishes. If the player ignores her warnings, or just inherits the Frenzied Flame without speaking with her, she will say that The Tarnished is no longer fit, ending her accord, and forever leaving their side but threatening to kill them should they become Lord of Chaos. If the Tarnished instead heeds her warnings, Melina and the protagonist will continue their Journey for the Flame of Ruin.

sources.title: The Tarnished (Protagonist)
sources.text:
A Tarnished of no renown, called to cross the sea of fog to the Lands Between, having been blessed once more by the Grace once thought lost to their kind. Their origins are unknown, as are their accomplishments prior to their arrival in the Lands Between.
The Tarnished begins their journey in the Chapel of Anticipation, off the western coast of Limgrave, where they find only the corpse of a Finger Maiden slumped against a wall. After a brief encounter with a Grafted Scion, the Tarnished falls from the precipice and washes up in the Stranded Graveyard. Although death seems inevitable, they are found by a mysterious woman riding a spectral steed. The woman grants the Tarnished two flasks: one of crimson tears and the other of cerulean tears. With these blessings, the Tarnished emerges from the damp cavern into the grasslands of Limgrave.
The Tarnished is reunited with the woman once more, and she introduces herself to them as Melina. Seeing that the Tarnished is maidenless, she offers to play the role of a Finger Maiden, allowing the Tarnished to convert the Runes they collect from their enemies into strength. In return, she requests that the Tarnished bring her with them to the foot of the Erdtree. To aid them further, Melina grants the Tarnished a whistle which will allow them to call upon her spectral steed, who's name she reveals to be Torrent. Melina further explains to the Tarnished that she is searching for a purpose given to her by her mother inside the Erdtree long ago, and the reason she lives, despite her burnt and spectral state. She advises the Tarnished to seek the Great Runes: shards of the shattered Elden Ring currently held by the Demigods.
